summary: Log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game
description: The bug I m just moving around in my jungle world while trying to record a youtube video. Windows that were open are chrome, obs, sticky notes, streamlabs obs, and the minecraft launcher, as well as the game The game will crash after moving around a little bit. Very lagging in the jungle, the log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game. Reproduce - Create a superflat world of jungle biome, and fly freely on the world. minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake - Using spawn eggs to spawn very many parrots. - Use the following command tp e[type parrot] p Here is the crash report: 19w40a: [ crash-2019-10-03_23.59.03-client.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.NullPointerException: Ticking entity at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at akm.ab(SourceFile:301) at akn.ab(SourceFile:228) at akd.h(SourceFile:399) at akm.h(SourceFile:2059) at akn.h(SourceFile:295) at atk.h(SourceFile:34) at dmr.a(SourceFile:165) at bjk.a(SourceFile:648) at dmr.g(SourceFile:136) at das.n(SourceFile:1389) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new superflat world with the following settings:
   - Layers: `minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block`
   - Biome: `minecraft:jungle`
   - Features: `biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake`

2. Enter Creative mode by typing `/gamemode creative` in the chat.

3. Use spawn eggs to spawn a large number of parrots around you (at least 50).

4. Type the command `/tp @e[type=parrot] ~ ~ ~` into the chat to teleport all spawned parrots to your location.

5. Move around freely within the world for at least a few minutes, observing if the game becomes very laggy and the log repeatedly prints "Ticking entity".

6. Observe whether the game crashes after moving around and experiencing significant lag.

7. Take screenshots highlighting any lag or unusual behavior observed during this process.

8. Exit the game and gather the `debug` folder from `.minecraft`.

9. Attach the screenshots and debug ZIP to your report for further analysis.
Observed Behavior:
When moving around in a jungle world while recording a YouTube video, the game becomes very laggy and eventually crashes. During this process, the log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity." At the time of the crash, several applications were open, including Chrome, OBS, Sticky Notes, Streamlabs OBS, and the Minecraft launcher. The issue can be reproduced by creating a superflat world with a jungle biome using the following command: `minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake`. To exacerbate the problem, use spawn eggs to generate many parrots and execute the command `/tp @e[type=parrot] p` repeatedly. The crash report indicates a `java.lang.NullPointerException` related to ticking an entity, as shown in the stack trace provided.

This detailed description should help developers understand the specific conditions under which the bug occurs and assist them in diagnosing and fixing the issue.
Expected Behavior: When moving around in a superflat jungle world with many parrots, the game should remain stable and not crash. The log should not repeatedly print "Ticking entity," and gameplay should proceed smoothly without any lag or performance issues.
